title: Tashkent Rising Revisited
premise: Elodie Thornbury, a whistle-blower living under four names, discovers her safe house has been listed for sale online — with interior photos that expose her hiding place, her documents, and the faces of two other protected witnesses. The listing is bait set by a fixer working for three governments who all want the same leaked dossier buried before Frankfurt markets open in seventy-two hours. Hunted by an assassin who once spared her, Elodie must move the truth through smugglers, journalists, and one honest regulator, trading each of her four identities like currency. In the end she burns every alias, testifies by proxy at dawn as the markets open, and walks into a new life with no name at all — free because she is finally findable.
about_author: Tamsin Underhill is the pen name of a former financial-crimes analyst who spent six years inside compliance departments across three countries before walking away. She writes thrillers about people who know exactly how systems fail, because she has watched them do it.

chapters.title: The House That Should Not Exist
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Scrolling property listings for surveillance practice, she finds her own safe house photographed room by room — including the hidden drawer where her real documents sleep. Emotional beat: cold recognition that invisibility was always rented, never owned.

chapters.title: Four Names, One Woman
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter establishing her aliases: Marion Voss, Katrin Aal, Sister Bernadette, and Elodie Thornbury herself. Her POV, tracing how each identity was built to survive a different betrayal. Emotional beat: grief for the woman she was before the first name change.

chapters.title: Seventy-Two Hours to Frankfurt
chapters.summary: Elodie confirms the listing went live eleven hours ago; the ECB announcement drops Friday. Her handler, a burned-out MI6 exile called Pell, warns her the photos mean someone inside protection sold her. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Buyer Who Isn't Buying
chapters.summary: Elodie poses as a prospective buyer to meet the estate agent, a nervous intermediary named Okafor. His client list points to a shell company tied to the very bank her dossier indicts. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt returning after years of stillness.

chapters.title: What the Dossier Says
chapters.summary: Her POV unpacking the leak: sanctioned money laundered through Central Asian infrastructure projects, blessed by officials in three governments. Emotional beat: the weight of knowing, and how knowledge has cost her everyone she loved.

chapters.title: The Assassin's Morning
chapters.summary: POV shift to Marek, the assassin hired to retrieve the dossier — the man who let her live in Vilnius five years ago. He studies her old photo and hesitates. Emotional beat: professional detachment cracking around an old debt.

chapters.title: Sister Bernadette Dies First
chapters.summary: Elodie torches the convent identity: burns papers, alerts the abbess, watches from a bus stop as watchers arrive too late. Emotional beat: ritual mourning — killing a version of yourself to save what remains.

chapters.title: Pell's Ledger
chapters.summary: Pell reveals the protection program was compromised from within; he gives her a list of three possible traitors, one of whom may be him. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against arithmetic — trust no one, but you cannot run alone.

chapters.title: The Journalist Who Owes Her
chapters.summary: In Leipzig, Elodie contacts Lena Brandt, an investigative reporter whose career Elodie once saved with an anonymous tip. Lena agrees to hold a copy of the dossier. Emotional beat: cautious hope that truth can have allies.

chapters.title: Marek Closes In
chapters.summary: Marek traces the estate agent to Okafor, squeezes him gently, and learns Elodie passed through Leipzig. He reports a false location to buy time — or so he tells himself. Emotional beat: complicity growing roots.

chapters.title: Katrin Aal's Last Train
chapters.summary: Elodie rides night rails toward Frankfurt under her German alias, memorizing faces, rehearsing dead drops. A ticket inspector lingers too long. Emotional beat: exhaustion wearing the mask of calm.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Voice
chapters.summary: A phone call from a friendly voice inside the protection program offers extraction — using details only the leaker could know. Elodie records it. Emotional beat: betrayal confirmed, and strangely clarifying.

chapters.title: Frankfurt Before Dawn
chapters.summary: She reaches Frankfurt and caches copies of the dossier in three places: a bank locker, a church, and Lena's hands. Emotional beat: the relief of redundancy — truth that survives any single death.

chapters.title: Markets, Men, and Money
chapters.summary: POV of Deputy Minister Havelka, one of the three governments' fixers, briefing brokers on how to absorb bad news quietly. He mentions a woman with four names. Emotional beat: banality of institutional evil.

chapters.title: The Locker Trap
chapters.summary: Elodie checks the bank locker early and finds it already opened — Marek got there first but left the contents untouched, plus a note: 'Vilnius isn't paid yet.' Emotional beat: terror braided with gratitude.

chapters.title: Okafor's Confession
chapters.summary: Okafor, terrified, admits the listing was ordered by a private intelligence firm, Corvid Solutions, contracted by all three governments simultaneously. Emotional beat: small man's courage, costly and late.

chapters.title: Marion Voss Walks Into a Police Station
chapters.summary: Elodie uses her Dutch alias to file a formal complaint against Corvid, forcing a paper trail the governments must acknowledge. Emotional beat: using the system's own machinery as a weapon.

chapters.title: Marek's Debt
chapters.summary: Marek's POV: flashback to Vilnius, why he let her go — she had shown him his own name on a kill list he never knew existed. Emotional beat: the assassin realizing he has been a tool twice over.

chapters.title: Lena Under Pressure
chapters.summary: Security services visit Lena's newsroom with legal threats. She moves the dossier to a foreign editor and lies beautifully. Emotional beat: press freedom as a physical act of defiance.

chapters.title: The Intermediary Summit
chapters.summary: Havelka offers Elodie immunity and silence via back channels; Pell urges her to take it. She refuses on a recorded line. Emotional beat: the loneliness of saying no to safety.

chapters.title: Corvid's Cleaners
chapters.summary: Corvid deploys a second team; a safe house in Rotterdam burns with her supposed belongings inside. Elodie watches the news footage of 'her' death. Emotional beat: eerie liberation — officially, she is already dead.

chapters.title: The Honest Regulator
chapters.summary: Elodie identifies one incorruptible BaFin examiner, Dr. Anselm Roth, and requests an emergency meeting through coded correspondence. Emotional beat: betting everything on one stranger's integrity.

chapters.title: Roth's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Roth's POV: he reads enough of the dossier to understand the scale, and understands what it will cost his career and possibly his family. Emotional beat: ordinary conscience confronting extraordinary pressure.

chapters.title: Midnight Exchange
chapters.summary: Elodie and Roth meet in a printing plant; she gives him authenticated originals, he gives her a sworn statement timeline. Marek watches from the gantry and does not intervene. Emotional beat: handoff of trust between strangers.

chapters.title: Pell's Choice
chapters.summary: Pell is confronted by his old service and ordered to deliver Elodie. Instead he sends them her false coordinates and prepays his own exile. Emotional beat: redemption purchased with ruin.

chapters.title: The Second Assassin
chapters.summary: Corvid's cleaner, Voss-killer Ilsa Rehn, catches Elodie's scent through the police complaint. A near-miss in a tram tunnel leaves Elodie wounded. Emotional beat: fear stripped of romance — being hunted hurts.

chapters.title: Stitches and Strategy
chapters.summary: A retired forger named Bem patches Elodie's shoulder and proposes the boldest move: publish everything publicly, making suppression pointless. Emotional beat: desperation maturing into audacity.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Deadline
chapters.summary: Havelka, his British counterpart, and a Central Asian minister convene secretly; they authorize extreme measures if the dossier surfaces before the open. Emotional beat: cold institutional calculus over human lives.

chapters.title: Marek Breaks
chapters.summary: Ordered to kill Elodie by sunrise, Marek instead delivers Corvid's operational files to Roth anonymously — paying his Vilnius debt in full. Emotional beat: an assassin choosing which side of history to stand on.

chapters.title: The Leak Goes Live
chapters.summary: At 4 a.m., a partner outlet publishes the dossier's core findings. Markets futures wobble. Elodie, bandaged, watches screens in Bem's basement. Emotional beat: vertigo — the secret is a secret no more.

chapters.title: Rehn's Last Contract
chapters.summary: Ilsa Rehn, contract voided by publication, hunts Elodie anyway — for reputation. A rooftop chase across Frankfurt ends with Rehn arrested by police tipped off by Marek. Emotional beat: fury giving way to grim satisfaction.

chapters.title: Havelka Unravels
chapters.summary: With the story public, Havelka's government disavows him; he shreds documents and books a flight that will never board. Elodie's recorded refusal call becomes evidence. Emotional beat: justice arriving sideways, imperfectly.

chapters.title: Roth Opens the File
chapters.summary: Dr. Roth formally opens enforcement proceedings as trading begins; the implicated bank's shares halve by mid-session. Emotional beat: quiet triumph of procedure wielded bravely.

chapters.title: Testimony by Proxy
chapters.summary: Unable to appear safely, Elodie submits sworn testimony through Roth and Lena under seal, her four names attached as corroboration. Emotional beat: reclaiming authorship of her own history.

chapters.title: Pell Found
chapters.summary: Pell is detained at a Baltic border crossing; his sacrifice exposed. Elodie must decide whether to burn her last alias to testify for him. Emotional beat: love versus survival, finally not opposed.

chapters.title: The Name She Keeps
chapters.summary: Elodie chooses to surface as Elodie Thornbury — the only name she chose herself — and gives a guarded interview to Lena. Emotional beat: identity as an act of will, not a hiding place.

chapters.title: Corvid Falls
chapters.summary: Parliamentary hearings gut Corvid Solutions; Okafor testifies safely; the estate agent who listed her house turns out to be a coerced witness, now freed. Emotional beat: the machine dismantled bolt by bolt.

chapters.title: What Justice Costs
chapters.summary: Roth wins sanctions but key ministers resign quietly into consultancy jobs — accountability incomplete. Elodie rages, then accepts partial victory as the only kind there is. Emotional beat: mature disillusionment without despair.

chapters.title: Pell Comes Home
chapters.summary: Charges against Pell dropped thanks to her testimony; they meet in person for the first time since the safe house listing, both changed. Emotional beat: two survivors recognizing each other without masks.

chapters.title: Tashkent Rising
chapters.summary: Epilogue. Months later, Elodie — under her one true name — consults for witness-protection reform inspired by the Central Asian cases. The final image: a new property listing, ordinary and unphotographed, and her walking through an open front door. Emotional beat: peace earned, guarded, and real.
